articles.title: Dave Franco and the Cast of Idiots Break Down the Comedy's Most Explosive Scene
articles.summary: Dave Franco, Mason Thames, O’Shea Jackson Jr., Kiernan Shipka, and director Macon Blair unpack the upcoming comedy Idiots, discussing its title change, shocking twists, and explosive moments.
body: Idiots, the new comedy starring Dave Franco, O’Shea Jackson Jr., Mason Thames, and Kiernan Shipka, has a little bit of everything: a star-studded cast, a bone-chilling villainous turn, and Dave Franco performing in what he calls a “top three ‘shit yourself’ scene in cinematic history.”

The upcoming movie, written and directed by Macon Blair (The Toxic Avenger, I Don’t Feel At Home in This World Anymore), tells the story of what happens “when two unqualified bozos (Franco, Jackson) are hired to transfer a rich teen (Thames) to rehab [and] their straightforward gig quickly spirals into dangerous mayhem.”

I sat down with Blair and the cast for an exclusive roundtable interview to unpack all of the movie’s big moments (many comedic, some filled with drama verging on horror) and dive into the challenges of bringing an ambitious story with a stacked cast to the big screen on a limited budget.

One of the biggest hurdles Blair encountered when making Idiots was what exactly to call it. The film was originally titled (and marketed as) The Shitheads. Blair says that, despite what you might think, it wasn’t outside pressure that forced the name change.
points: Dave Franco, Mason Thames, O’Shea Jackson Jr., Kiernan Shipka, and director Macon Blair unpack the upcoming comedy Idiots, discussing its title change, shocking twists, and explosive moments.

articles.title: The Folio Society Reveals The Three-Body Problem Trilogy: Remembrance of Earth's Past
articles.summary: Liu Cixin's The Three-Body Problem trilogy is widely regarded as one of the best science fiction epics of the modern era, and that story has reached an even wider audience lately thanks to the Netflix series.
body: The Three-Body Problem Trilogy: Remembrance of Earth's Past collects all three books in the series - The Three-Body Problem, The Dark Forest, and Death's End. The book features art and design work by Griffin and includes a brand-new introduction by the author never before published in English.

“Starting with the Chinese Cultural Revolution and spanning some 18 million years into the future, Liu Cixin's masterpiece is as broad as it is compelling,” said Folio Society Editor James Rose in a statement. “A tale of humanity's struggle, and that of a civilisation fighting for its very existence, this dares to answer the question: 'Are we alone in the Universe?'. Beautifully and brilliant evoked in Matt Griffin's artwork, this is the ultimate edition of a science-fiction phenomenon. Fans of the series, anyone interested in sci-fi and hard science, and new readers alike will be awestruck by this edition.”

articles.title: New Indie Fishing Game Is More Popular Than Modern Warfare 4 Beta On Steam
articles.summary: Everyone has heard of Call of Duty, and yet, a video game that you've probably never heard of is outperforming the first Modern Warfare 4 beta on Steam. How to Fish looks like a surprise hit with over 341,000 concurrent players today, per Steam.
body: That easily tops the early-access beta for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, which hit just over 115,000 concurrent players Friday on Steam and has been declining since then. Keep in mind this first trial with the newest entry in the FPS franchise is for people who preordered Modern Warfare on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S. An open beta is set to begin this upcoming weekend, from August 28 to September 1.

Meanwhile, How to Fish is a physics-based game about reeling in cod and sharks, then beating them to death by any means necessary. That includes punching the water dwellers, stabbing them, and even no-scope shooting them for more money. So yes, it falls on the silly side compared to a more realistic simulator.

Intriguingly, How to Fish has the support of Evil Landfall, the publishing and support side of Peak developer Landfall. That co-op climbing game was one of last year's biggest surprise hits on Steam. Both titles fall under the newish genre called friendslop.

articles.title: Samsung's Absolutely Massive 57" Dual 4K Gaming Monitor Drops to the Lowest Price I've Ever Seen
articles.summary: For a very limited time, the biggest and baddest gaming monitor you can possibly get (short of getting a TV) has dropped to its lowest price ever. Samsung via its official store is offering the massive 57" Samsung Odyssey Neo G9 Dual 4K UHD gaming monitor for $1,349.99 with free shipping.
body: The 57" Samsung Odyssey Neo G9 is one of few 57" dual 4K UHD monitors on the market, boasting an eye-watering 7680x2160 resolution, or the equivalent of two 4K UHD monitors stacked next to each other. Despite the display being so large, it has an above-average 140ppi pixel density, which is amazing considering the fact that in general the bigger the display, the lower the ppi. To put that into perspective, it's as sharp as a 32" 4K monitor. Wow.

The Odyssey Neo G9 is equipped with a Mini LED backlight paired with a quantum dot (QLED) panel. Like its namesake suggests, mini-LED panels have smaller LEDs than traditional LED LCD monitors, so you can squeeze in more lighting zones. Mini-LED monitors are also much brighter than OLED monitors, which is very important because larger monitors are generally dimmer than smaller ones to start. Local dimming combined with higher brightness improves contrast ratio and HDR and is also useful in overpowering glare and reflections.
points: For a very limited time, the biggest and baddest gaming monitor you can possibly get (short of getting a TV) has dropped to its lowest price ever.

articles.summary: CD Projekt Red has narrowed down the release timing for The Witcher 4, confirming the RPG is coming sometime in 2028. The company revealed this in a new video that sets the table for Gamescom this week.
body: There won't be any Witcher 4 news at Gamescom, but CD Projekt Red will highlight The Witcher 3's new Songs of the Past DLC at the showcase, while there will be "a surprise or two to share" during livestreams planned throughout Gamescom.

More than 500 people are working on The Witcher 4 now, CD Projekt Red joint-CEO Michal Nowakowski said in a newly released video. "This is our biggest, boldest, and most ambitious game to date," he said.
As for the 2028 release date for The Witcher 4, Nowakowski said, "I know it's a bit of a wait, and you'd love to play it sooner--but let the team cook. It will be worth the wait."

The Witcher 4 kicks off a new trilogy of The Witcher games, which will also include The Witcher 5 and The Witcher 6. These will all be released within a six-year window, so the whole new trilogy could be out by 2034.

articles.title: GTA 6 Leak Shows Off Apparent Nudist Colony
articles.summary: A new clip showing leaked Grand Theft Auto 6 footage has made its way online, and it looks like you're going to be able to visit a nudist colony in Leonida. The clip, which just runs for a few minutes, shows co-protagonist Jason walking near a pool and several hot tubs, with dozens of naked people…
body: Some of them seem relatively neutral to Jason's presence, while others are annoyed with the completely clothed man walking around and looking at them with binoculars. That seems like a reasonable reaction. One woman in particular notices Jason leering with binoculars and physically attacks him. Again, reasonable.

While we've seen a whole bunch of GTA 6 clips from a still-at-large leaker over the last week, they may not have a particularly negative effect on Rockstar. According to a former technical director at the studio, the vast majority of players don't care about the leaked footage, and it pales in comparison to the controversial Hot Coffee incident that affected Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. Still, Take-Two is actively subpoenaing information related to the leaks in an effort to uncover the leaker's identity.
We'll get our first official look at gameplay on August 27, exclusively on Netflix. Grand Theft Auto 6 launches for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19.

articles.title: Vampire Survivors Gets Bloodier and Raunchier In This Wild New Game
articles.summary: Blood Dungeon is a chaotic riff on Vampire Survivors that trades in depth for high-score chasing buffoonery.
body: Here’s a two-word video game review for you: Blood Dungeon. That’s it. That’s the review.

No, really, what more do you need me to say? It’s a video game called Blood Dungeon. Bless developer Messhof, the studio behind Nidhogg and Wheel World, for giving its latest game a title that tells you exactly what you’re getting with this lo-fi Vampire Survivors riff upfront. It’s like seeing a store-brand cereal called Sugar Balls. No confusion about what’s in that box! As it says on the tin, Blood Dungeon is about as lowbrow as video games get — and that’s exactly what I ordered. It’s a proudly crude roguelike built for a generation raised on Adult Swim. Sometimes, you just crave something that dares to be stupid.
points: Blood Dungeon is a chaotic riff on Vampire Survivors that trades in depth for high-score chasing buffoonery.

articles.title: GTA 6 Leaks Don’t Matter, So Please Calm Down, Ex-Rockstar Director Says
articles.summary: Former Rockstar North director Obbe Vermeij has commented on the many GTA 6 leaks that have emerged over the past week. Vermeij, who was the technical director for GTA 3, GTA: San Andreas, GTA 4, and other titles in the series, told everyone to "clam down" because "the leaks are a nothing burger."…
body: He said Rockstar is intentionally staying quiet as part of the company's marketing strategy to generate as much hype as possible for GTA 6, and the leaks are not prompting Rockstar to amend its plans. That's no surprise, as a recent report specifically said Rockstar was not going to alter its marketing plans for GTA 6 due to the spate of leaks coming to light. The Netflix premiere of the game's "extended look" remains scheduled for August 27.

Vermeij said the leaks are no big deal in part because "90% of future players don't spend their time on the internet looking for video snippets." He added, "They don't have the time and don't want spoilers."
He went on to say the development teams working on GTA 6 are probably "a little annoyed about [the leaks] but not more than that."

Vermeij pointed out that he was working at Rockstar the time of the infamous "Hot Coffee" situation surrounding GTA: San Andreas. He said this was a "nightmare" for Rockstar's management team in New York, but didn't affect the developers themselves in Edinburgh at Rockstar North.

articles.title: New D&D Book Gives Every Class More Magic and Pets to Play With
articles.summary: After the “new era” of Dungeons & Dragons kicked off with Ravenloft: The Horrors Within, Wizards of the Coast has a very different type of product lined up to follow the latest excursion into the dreaded mists of its horror setting.
body: Polygon had the chance to read and review both products early, and together they reaffirm the current design philosophy of 2024’s 5.5 edition of the game. Arcana Unleashed goes a long way toward fixing some subclasses that were lackluster in 5e, and it gives more magic-focused options to players. In the process, it also erodes the barriers between classes, offering more flexibility for each class at the expense of what makes each distinct to begin with. Whether you like it or not, that’s D&D’s current direction.

Of course, this being a book about magic, wizard subclasses are treated with extreme care. Players now get all the magic school options that were missing from the Player’s Handbook, namely Conjurer, Necromancer, Enchanter, and Transmuter. They all receive significant boosts compared to their 5e versions. The Conjurer now gets their teleportation ability at level 3 rather than 6, and for a number of times equal to their Intelligence modifier, making this wizard very hard to catch on the battlefield. At level 6, the Conjurer’s summoned creatures become stronger, with temporary hit points and resistance to most forms of damage.

articles.title: Guy Richie’s Netflix Crime Series Is So Good It’s Already Been Renewed
articles.summary: Guy Ritchie is taking over streaming. The director of Snatch and Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels has hit shows on almost every service, with Young Sherlock on Prime Video, MobLand on Paramount Plus, and The Gentlemen on Netflix.
body: “The ambition of The Gentlemen has accelerated, the world has expanded and the consequences carry weight,” Ritchie said in a statement. “A third season felt inevitable, and I’m looking forward to pushing the boundaries of it further.”

The series follows Duke Eddie Honniman (Theo James), a former Army captain and United Nations peacekeeping officer who returns home after his father’s death to try to save the family estate. Eddie discovers that his dad had been letting a drug dealer operate a cannabis farm on the estate, and that his older brother Freddy (Daniel Ings) is deep in debt to a different dealer. While he at first just wants to make enough money off the illicit business to get his family out of trouble, Eddie becomes increasingly ambitious. By the end of the season, he’d formalized a partnership with Susie Glass (Kaya Scodelario) to help run her father’s criminal syndicate.

articles.title: The people of video games on what gives them cause for hope
articles.summary: Hello and welcome to one of our final pieces for Optimism Week here on Eurogamer. This time, we've turned to the industry itself for some answers, and as such I'm going to do my best to get out of the way as quickly as possible.
body: For this piece, we contacted a range of developers and general people-of-video-games to ask them one question: despite everything, what still gives you reason for optimism?
"It's a rough time for the games industry but a golden age for the game dev community.

"I've seen a tremendous outpouring of support for people after layoffs and for new writers trying to break in. It's moving to see the way people rally around their colleagues to raise money, find jobs, offer feedback on resumes and portfolios.

We game devs have always looked out for each other - passing the hat in hard times and mentoring new writers. But now, there's a renewed sense of responsibility and empathy for our colleagues. That feeling, that shared care and desire to help each other out, that's how we win. And it gives me hope for our future."

articles.title: 'GTA 6' Leaks Confirm Rockstar's Raunchiest Game Yet With Shocking New Clips
articles.summary: Rockstar isn't one to shy away from sex, and the latest Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks prove it. The hacking group behind the unauthorized footage has begun to focus on the more risqué aspects of the game, and so far, it looks like the open-world sequel is upping the ante.
body: On Aug. 22, hacking group Cyberleek continued sharing gameplay clips shilling a crypto coin that has reportedly earned at least six figures. Specifically, the hackers teased that, if their crypto coin reached a $3 million market cap, they would release strip club footage. GTA 6 fans blew through the market cap goal within hours. Cyberleek promptly uploaded a clip of GTA 6 protagonist Jason walking into an exotic dance club.

Watching the clip may be difficult because publisher Take-Two quickly removes social media posts that contain the footage. Thanks to reports online, however, we've still learned a few things about how Rockstar is implementing the feature. For example, players cannot use weapons inside the establishment, but there's plenty to keep them busy regardless — like a pool mini-game. If the player stands still for long enough, the game will switch to a cinematic camera. The workers have some elaborate dances, many of which show off the game's jiggle physics.
points: Rockstar isn't one to shy away from sex, and the latest Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks prove it.
The hacking group behind the unauthorized footage has begun to focus on the more risqué aspects of the game, and so far, it looks like the open-world sequel is upping the ante.

articles.title: "I want to keep pouring my energy into game creation going forward" - Hideo Kojima still wants to make games even at 63
articles.summary: Hideo Kojima - known as the director of the Death Stranding and Metal Gear Solid series - celebrated his 63rd birthday recently. Don't worry though, he's not interested in retiring just yet.
body: In a big post made to X, Kojima shared his thoughts on his career moving forward alongside a video of the Lumens statue in the Kojima Productions office. He wrote: "I've turned 63. As the years pile on, the things I 'must do' and the things I 'want to do' just keep multiplying. At the same time, the 'time I have available' keeps shrinking. I need to constantly scrutinize how I spend my time and how I live my life (my way of being).

"That said, once I've shouldered a burden, I can't just leave it behind. This year marks the 40th anniversary since I first started making games. It's also the 10th anniversary of founding Kojipro. From late October through the end of the year, we're planning to hold the 'Kojipro Exhibition,' at the Azabudai Hills Gallery. Even the entrance Ludens has been updated to the '10th Anniversary Ludens' version. Amid all sorts of opportunities and offers coming my way, I want to keep pouring my energy into game creation going forward. Looking forward to your continued support."
points: Hideo Kojima - known as the director of the Death Stranding and Metal Gear Solid series - celebrated his 63rd birthday recently.
